_note: SL-008 review m3 and m4 (the class 'C# spellings that set a shell verb or request elevation', and the ways of attaching a manifest) and M2 (who calls the rescan start), closed as their classes. The rules are the settled entries of .taad/fitness.yaml under '# settled by SL-008', read from there by RescanElevationRulesCorpusTests (their only copy). Each class is bounded by who produces its members, which is whoever edits src, a project file or the window hook next, by accident or in a hurry, not to get past a rule. A row is a snippet of one to three lines: expect 'fire' means some pattern of the rule matches it, 'quiet' that none does. 'before' is what the patterns the design wrote (listed under 'beforePatterns') did with the row, and the test recomputes it from them on every run, so the rows the fix closes stay shown: a row that was 'quiet' and now fires is one the fix closed, and a row that was 'fire' and is now 'quiet' is an over-broad match the fix lifted. The rules the design did not have (the manifest, the call-site and the hook entries) had no patterns before: every row's 'before' is 'quiet'.
